title: SLO-anchored decision curve optimizer for canary interruptions
creator: Aisha Romero
description: Build a decision-curve based controller that converts multi-signal SLO deviations into an interpretable, tunable interrupt score used by canary and A/B flows. Unlike simple threshold triggers, the decision curve optimizer composes percentile-aware signals (latency P50/P95, top-line error rate, token cost per request, throughput) into a normalized curve with hysteresis and dwell controls so we can safely interrupt or drain traffic during regressions while minimizing false positives.
acceptance_criteria: Controller computes a single interrupt_score in [0,100] combining at least latency P95, error_rate, token_cost_per_request, and throughput delta.
Interrupt score mapping is configurable via decision curve parameters (shape, knee location, signal weights, normalization) from Console and API.

When interrupt_score >= 75 for a sustained dwell window (configurable, default 90s) the system triggers a traffic-interruption action (scale-down canary traffic by 50% or failover to baseline model) and writes an event to audit logs.
Controller supports percentile-windowing (rolling windows per cohort) and uses cohort-aware baselining so noisy low-volume cohorts do not cause global interrupts.
End-to-end e2e test covering a synthetic regression (latency + cost spike) demonstrates automated partial evacuation and rollback signal recorded in model rollout timeline.
Performance overhead < 2% CPU on routing plane and < 5ms added latency to decision path in the common case.
technical_design: We will implement a lightweight decision curve composed of three stages: 1) signal normalization: convert each metric to a score in [0,1] using robust baselines (median/robust stddev and configurable percentiles), 2) per-signal shaping: apply monotonic shaping functions (linear, log, and soft-knee) and optional cost-normalization for token-cost, 3) fusion and hysteresis: weighted sum -> percentile transform -> hysteresis + minimum dwell. Fusion uses a cost-normalized z-score so token-cost increases weigh proportionally to latency regressions. Configuration model stored in runtime-config with safe defaults. Autotune will be an offline Bayesian optimization job that suggests signal weights and knee locations using labeled historical rollouts. The controller exposes a debug endpoint for decision curve visualization and an explainability payload (top-3 contributing signals) in the rollout audit event.
rollout_plan: Phase A: feature-flagged rollout to internal staging with synthetic probes (2 weeks). Phase B: open to 5% canaries across low-traffic customers with read-only shadow mode (no traffic interruption) and telemetry collection (2 weeks). Phase C: enable interrupt actions for internal traffic only and run a short experiment comparing manual aborts vs automated interruptions. Phase D: gradual ramp to 25% across production with on-call playbook and rollback override (2 engineers on-call). Each phase gated by experiment success metrics and a safety checklist.
monitoring_and_alerting: Create per-canary dashboards: interrupt_score timeseries, contributing signal breakdown, dwell windows, action events, and false positive counter. Alert rules: interrupt_score_spike_alert (P95 > 80 for 2 windows) -> page on-call; unexpected_eviction_rate > 0.5% -> notify PM/Eng. All actions must emit structured audit logs with rollback_reason, top_signals, and pre/post traffic distribution.
experiments: Shadow blending: compare shadow_score vs live_score to estimate action precision before enabling interrupts.
Weight search: offline BO job to find weights that maximize true-positive detection while keeping false positives < 1% on historical rollouts.
Hysteresis ablation: A/B different dwell durations (60s vs 180s) to observe time-to-detection vs false positive tradeoff.
Cohort isolation: measure benefit of cohort-aware baselining vs global baselining on low-volume customer cohorts.
decisions: Use an additive weighted fusion with a subsequent percentile transform rather than a pure multiplicative anomaly score to keep interpretability high.
Default interrupt action is a partial canary drain (reduce canary route to 10% and re-route 40% to baseline model) instead of full abort to reduce blast radius.
Autotune will run offline for now; manual approve of suggested parameters required before applying to production configuration.
open_questions: What storage and TTL for historical baselines per cohort (keep too long increases staleness; too short increases noise)?
Should token-cost be converted to per-token or per-request basis for fusion? We default to per-request normalized by median tokens but want feedback.
How to represent composite explainability payload to downstream SREs while keeping events compact? Current plan is top-3 signals + magnitudes.
